html:
A state in north China founded in 304 by Liu Yuan, a noble of the Southern Xiongnu, and destroyed in 329. It was the first of the Sixteen Kingdoms, and the map shows it in 300 in what is now Shanxi and the Ordos.

Liu Yuan's family had taken the Han imperial surname through old marriage ties between the Xiongnu and the Han dynasty, so he named his state Han and presented himself as the Han's heir. He used the chaos of the Jin civil wars to break away. His son Liu Cong sent armies that sacked Luoyang in 311 and captured the Jin emperor. This Yongjia disaster set off a flight of northern Chinese to the south. Chang'an fell in 316.

In 319 the ruler Liu Yao renamed the state Zhao. A former general, Shi Le, had already set up his own Later Zhao, and in 329 he destroyed Han Zhao.
